simon: Quick Q — planning a small contract tweak for model selection + routing hints on /v1/generate. Want to make sure we don't break older clients.

simon: Current plan: accept `model_select` (array) and `region_hint`/`tier_hint`. Include `served_model` in response so callers can log which exact variant served. Example request we propose:
```json
{
  "model_select": ["redwood-large-v2", "redwood-large-v1-compat"],
  "region_hint": "eu-west-1",
  "tier_hint": "dedicated",
  "fallback_policy": "compatible-variant"
}
```
Question: is adding a top-level `served_model` field a breaking change for SDKs/clients that parse responses as freeform JSON/strings? Or should we put it under `meta` or return it as a response header `X-Served-Model`?

lara: Short answer: most SDKs ignore extra fields, but a few legacy clients (mobile teams) do a strict parse into a struct. Putting it under `meta` reduces surprise, but header is safest for strict parsers. Either is fine if we document it and ship a minor semver bump for SDKs.

anya: Also need to consider compatibility when `model_select` includes models with different kv-cache layout / max_seq_len. We should validate selection server-side and skip incompatible variants rather than failing the request. That aligns with `fallback_policy=compatible-variant`.

kevin: Agreed on skip. For clarity, propose this behavior: 1) filter by region/tier capability, 2) filter by model shape compatibility, 3) pick first remaining model. If none remain -> 412 with structured error `no_compatible_model` and suggestion list. Keep old behavior as default (if `model` single string provided, keep exact-match semantics).

simon: That sounds good. For the error response shape, minimal is important. Example error we propose:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "no_compatible_model",
    "message": "No compatible variants available for requested model_select and hints",
    "suggested_alternatives": ["redwood-small-compat"]
  }
}
```

lara: One more subtlety: if we add `served_model` in response body, older API gateway caching might treat responses as different. Use a stable header would be safer for caches.

anya: Can we do both? header + `meta.served_model` for richer clients? Header first, and body meta added behind a feature flag `response.meta.served_model=true` for canary.

kevin: Yes -- feature flag makes rollout easier. We'll default to header only. Add integration test asserting header is present and body meta optional behind flag.

julie: FYI I'm picking up the SDK changes. Will add parsing for header `X-Served-Model` and add meta fallback. I'll open a PR and link here. @simon please add the API contract doc change in `docs/api/model-routing.md`.

simon: Pinged. PR for server: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1214 (draft). Please review. CI will run the compatibility suite.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for PR #1214 — build 9842. Unit tests 241/241, integration 18/20 (2 flaky tests skipped).

lara: Quick code-review notes: 1) make sure the 412 error uses top-level `error` object (we follow that pattern), 2) add an example to the spec showing `model_select` array with region/tier hints, 3) call out that `fallback_policy=none` will return 412 immediately.

anya: Also add a short runbook snippet: when a customer reports sudden model change logs, check `X-Served-Model` header and compare to rollout map. If meta field present, check `response.meta.rollout_id`.

kevin: Small ops ask — roll this behind canary for 48h on dedicated only, then widen. Feature flag name: `model_selection.served_model_meta` and `model_selection.header_enabled`.

julie: I'll add SDK tests and bump clients. ETA for PR review + SDK changes: EOD tomorrow if no blockers.

simon: Thanks all — next steps: 1) finalize server PR with header + optional meta behind flag, 2) lara to update docs, 3) julie to land SDK change, 4) canary for 48h. If anyone wants to be on the rollback pager, sign here.

anya: I'm on it :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll watch the canary metrics (latency / 412 rate)

lara: I'll update the API spec and post a short changelog in #docs when done.
